evals.prompt: Run analyzing-code on the working tree.
evals.expected_output: Tells the user the run can take hours because the mutation run executes the tests once per mutant. Records git status --porcelain and the short HEAD hash. Invokes measuring-code with 'from analyzing-code: paths ., root <root>, out <scratch-dir>, mutation all, install on failure, top 200', which writes the reports into <scratch-dir>/reports and summary.json into the scratch directory. Adds no dependency, report, or configuration file to the repository. Reads the code behind every entry analysis-rules.md names; a number alone is never a finding. The final message is the measurement report with headings Result, Scope, Code, Limits, Tools, Measurements, Findings, Skipped, at most 60 non-blank lines and at most 12 findings, each with finding kind, path:line, symbol, evidence, and an action from the fixed list. The Limits line holds the limits line of the measurement record.

evals.prompt: Measure the release/2.3 branch. This project has no mutation testing set up.
evals.expected_output: Confirms release/2.3 resolves with git rev-parse --verify --quiet 'release/2.3^{commit}', records its short hash, and adds a detached worktree under the scratch directory instead of checking out, stashing, or switching the working tree. Invokes measuring-code with the worktree as root and 'install first'. Reports the mutation measurement as skipped with the reason from the measurement record's mutation line, such as 'no mutation command', and lists it under Skipped. After the report is filled, removes the worktree with --force, prunes, and confirms git worktree list names no folder under the scratch directory.
The request is neither nothing nor one branch, tag, or commit name, so the skill asks one question: which one name to measure, or none for the working tree. It runs no measurement before the answer.
